landingPopulation.rule: B1123 (#443): every landing (impact + spellComplete) peaks at half the platform pool (constrained_presets.json spellParticlePool), so two overlapping landings, or 253's field beside one, fit; the rates below give each landing's schedule and SpellEffectsConfig::applyPool scales them to the peak. An exception is a landing the oracle fills with FEWER sprites: its peak is min(peakLive, half the pool).

sourceRecords.rule: B1131 (#451): the Source (cast) stage per measured row (survey id = the spells.eff record of the spell it was captured on; a spell takes the row of its spellsnew.eff record, animRecords, B1137), measured on the official client by the B1130 survey (review/B1130/anchor_table.tsv + record_table.tsv, fixed camera, caster heights above the feet). anchor: hands = the two hand bones, feet-ring = a ring at the feet rising lo->hi, orbit = an orbit of radius halfWidth over lo..hi (spiral: rising lo->hi), body = a cloud over lo..hi x +-halfWidth, head = a disc at the head bone (discLo..discHi, discShare of the sprites) with a column falling to lo. onset = seconds after BeginCast; holdOther / holdSelf = seconds the Source keeps emitting past OP_Action when the target is another entity / the caster (holdOther absent = self-only spell). B1150 (#470): a row carries NO shape any more -- every row's spell has a spellsnew.eff field-145 record, whose +0xA8 shape with dims +0xAC/+0xB0/+0xB4, offsets +0xB8/+0xBC/+0xC0, tilts +0xC4/+0xC8, depth bias +0xD0 and +0x19C scale draws the record's Source (the retired lo/hi/halfWidth/centroid + disc words are the bands in tests/spell_fx_shape_oracle.h, generated by refactor/B1150/scripts/gen_shape_bands.py); populations, sprite sizes, lifetimes, colour and alpha are each slot's spellsnew.edd emitter's (the rows' measured coverages are tests/spell_fx_population_oracle.h); the anchor and capture stay as evidence (hasShape is derived from the shape keys' absence, so a row without them is the default row: the style's own cloud). Rows: review/B1131/scripts/gen_source_records.py.

scale.why: B1120 scale (H 6.5 world units, entity anchor 3.6 above the feet); orbit 3.0 rad/s = B1122's record-23 orbit (54/656 castGlow override)

sourceRecords.defaultWhy: a record the survey did not reach, and a spell with no record: the style's own body cloud (B1122), the median onset of the 40 measured records and the median holdOther of the 28 other-target holds. B1145 (#465): a spellsnew.eff Source times each slot from spellsnew.edd (cast time + the cast-animation term for a +0x78 >= 0 emitter, else its fixed |+0x78|; +0x8C delay; +0x7C life), starting at this onset (the stage's measured latency); the rows carry no onset or hold (their measured values are tests/spell_fx_timing_oracle.h)
sourceRecords.overrideRecordsWhy: the row (animRecords of spells_us.txt field 145) of every spell with a spellOverrides row (the pool rule needs the Source hold of its record)

targetRecords.rule: B1132 (#452): the Target (landing) stage per measured row (survey id; a spell takes the row of its spellsnew.eff record, animRecords, B1137), measured on the official client by the B1130 survey (review/B1130/anchor_table.tsv target_anchor + the landing ROI's RUN line, target heights above the target's feet). The landing (impact + spellComplete) is drawn on the cast's TARGET, never on the caster of an other-target cast, except anchor caster. anchor: body = the style's B1120 volume on the target; caster = that volume round the CASTER whatever the target (27 PB-AE, measured; 8/9/11/19/43 self-only); head = a cloud over lo..hi x +-halfWidth placed relative to the target's HEAD bone (boneAt = the height the bone stands for) plus a glow at the bone (the face); feet = rings on the ground at the feet (radius halfWidth) rising lo->hi; column = a sheet falling from hi to lo over +-halfWidth. B1149 (#469): a row gives its record's landing SHAPE only -- populations, sprite sizes, lifetimes, art, colour and alpha are each Target slot's spellsnew.edd emitter's (the rows' measured coverages and the retired shaped-row populations are tests/spell_fx_population_oracle.h). Rows: review/B1132/scripts/gen_target_records.py.
targetRecords.defaultWhy: a record no row was captured on (B1137: a field-145 record with no row) and a spell with no record: the style's body volume on the target. B1145 (#465): a landing's slots take their timing from spellsnew.edd (fixed |+0x78| or +0x78, +0x8C delay, +0x7C life, from the landing styles' triggerDelay); the rows carry no onset or end (their measured values are tests/spell_fx_timing_oracle.h); B1150 (#470): no shape either -- every row's spell has a field-145 record, whose +0xA8..+0xD0 words draw the landing (the retired lo/hi/halfWidth/centroid bands: tests/spell_fx_shape_oracle.h)

animRecords.rule: B1137 (#457): the measured sourceRecords / targetRecords row a spell is drawn with is chosen by its spellsnew.eff record (spells_us.txt field 145), the record the official client draws (B1127), not by its spells.eff record (field 123). rows: field-145 record -> the row (survey id = the field-123 record of the spell that row was captured on: review/B1130/record_table.tsv spell_id; generator review/B1137/scripts/gen_anim_rows.py). A field-145 record with no row draws the default rows: a field-123 row was captured on a spell drawing a different field-145 record (1656 Thunderbold 145=85 vs 14 Strike 145=115, both 123=25), so it is no measurement of it. 93 (Breeze V2: 174 Clarity, 697 Breeze, 1287 Cassindra`s Chant) -> 6: record 93 is record 1 byte for byte but for ONE cell (Middle slot 0 attach code 5 vs 4), and the oracle draws 1287 (93) and 7 Hymn of Restoration (1) alike on a self cast (review/B1137/README.md sec. 3, leg A: Source cov 0.297/0.296, centroid 0.57/0.57). B1134 (#454): the discipline records 326/328/329/330 -> 51, measured by the OBSERVER rig on all four (review/B1134/README.md; their spellsnew.eff records differ only in name and colour words, and the oracle draws them alike in shape); record 325 (3 shadow knight spells: other textures and particle lifetimes) was not cast and draws the default rows.
